perplexity.description:
Released in 1997, Lost Highway (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) is a genre-defying compilation curated for David Lynch’s surreal thriller of the same name. The album blends electronic, jazz, and rock elements, reflecting the film’s dark, dreamlike atmosphere. Produced by Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails, the soundtrack features original compositions by Reznor, Angelo Badalamenti, and Barry Adamson, alongside tracks from prominent artists such as Marilyn Manson, David Bowie, Lou Reed, The Smashing Pumpkins, and Rammstein. The music ranges from industrial rock and ambient electronica to moody jazz and experimental soundscapes, creating a cohesive yet diverse listening experience that mirrors the film’s psychological tension and stylistic unpredictability.

As a collaborative effort by various artists, the album stands out in the discographies of its contributors for its unique fusion of styles and its association with Lynch’s visionary cinema. The soundtrack was both a critical and commercial success, reaching No. 7 on the Billboard 200 and earning Gold certification in the United States and Platinum in Canada. Its innovative approach to soundtrack composition and its influential roster of artists have cemented Lost Highway as a landmark release in the realm of film music, particularly within the electronic, jazz, and rock genres.
